Gold gains as Treasury yields stabilize, Nasdaq surges despite Fed tightening concerns - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices were higher in late U.S. trading Wednesday, while spot silver recovered from earlier losses, as a softer U.S. dollar and easing crude oil prices provided some support for precious metals despite persistent inflation concerns and expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. Strong corporate earnings lifted major U.S. stock indexes, while unresolved tensions involving Iran and the Strait of Hormuz continued to complicate the outlook for energy prices and monetary policy. Gold was trading near $4,141.01 an ounce, up 0.66%, while silver was near $57.976, up 0.34%, in the latest available late-session market readings. The latest U.S. economic reports continue to point to weakness in interest rate-sensitive sectors of the economy. September housing starts declined 5.2% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.221 million units , below expectations of approximately 1.305 million and down from an upwardly revised 1.288 million in August. Building permits slipped 0.2% to 1.400 million units, while single-family starts declined 4.6% to 859,000 units. Pending home sales fell 7.3% in September and 11.3% from a year earlier, reinforcing concerns that high mortgage rates and weakening household confidence are restraining residential investment. Wednesday's weekly U.S. petroleum inventory report also highlighted the continuing tightness in energy markets, with commercial crude oil stocks declining 3.1 million barrels to 412.5 million barrels, compared with expectations for a draw of approximately 300,000 barrels. Gasoline inventories fell 3.0 million barrels, while distillate stocks increased 1.7 million barrels.
